turns.narrator: It is early in April in the year 1883, and you wake to find Sherlock Holmes standing, fully dressed, by the side of your bed. The clock upon the mantelpiece shows a quarter-past seven. Holmes is, as a rule, a late riser, and you blink up at him in some surprise, and perhaps a touch of resentment, for you are yourself regular in your habits."Very sorry to knock you up, Watson," says he, "but it is the common lot this morning. Mrs. Hudson has been knocked up, she retorted upon me, and I on you." There is in his face that quiet alertness which tells you, even before he has spoken another word, that some singular business is afoot. No fire has been laid, but a client waits: a young lady who has arrived in a considerable state of excitement and insists upon seeing him in the sitting-room below. Should it prove to be an interesting case, he has called you so that you may follow it from the outset.The thin morning light lies cold upon the blind. Holmes stands ready at the door, and somewhere below, in the sitting-room, a frightened woman is waiting.Do you rise at once and go down with him?
